(This evening through Wednesday)...
Issued at 307 PM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Rest of this Afternoon and Tonight....

In the wake of the MCV organized convection now moving through parts 
of KY/OH, remnant showers will continue through late afternoon 
before stronger downward vertical motion ends precip chances for all 
but the far south by this evening. Copious mid-high clouds 
associated with convection over the southern Plains will keep any 
threat for fog development out of the question overnight. 

The remnant of the next in a chain of MCV's looks to move into the 
MS valley after 06Z, with some potential increase in light precip 
over the far western and southern portions of central Indiana 
towards 12Z. Meanwhile, surface analysis shows a backdoor cold front 
moving steadily southward through northern Indiana with temps 
falling at FWA recently. Have cut temps 1-2 cats late this afternoon 
and overnight along and north of I-70 to account for faster and 
further southward movement of the front compared to recent guidance. 

Thursday...

The back door frontal boundary should be draped near and possibly 
just south of I-70 by 12Z Thursday where it is expected to stall. 
Aforementioned next MCV is likely to move into central Indiana 
during the morning hours. Instability ahead of this feature looks 
meager. But increasing isentropic lift north-nw of the frontal 
boundary should support scattered showers with isolated 
thunderstorms with mucape up to 1000 J/KG.  Activity will push 
across much of central Indiana during the mid-late morning into 
early afternoon. Scattered surface based TS possible by mid-late 
afternoon along and south of the slowly advancing warm front. 
Complications to the forecast include any precip induced cold pool 
which may reinforce the frontal boundary location. This creates 
uncertainty regarding timing and location of surface based 
thunderstorms development and attendant severe weather threat. For 
now will keep all of central Indiana in the wording for marginal 
risk of severe weather in line with the most recent SWODY2. 

Thursday night and Friday... 

The focus for convection should diminish by midnight as the 3rd an 
final MCV moves east of central Indiana. However, the cold frontal 
boundary associated with southward moving shortwave through the 
western Great Lakes will support renewed shower development towards 
12Z Friday. In the wake of the frontal boundary, strong CAA will 
lead to gusty winds up to 30 mph with temps steady to slowing 
falling during the afternoon. Passage of the shortwave trough axis 
and increasing CAA aloft will support steeper lapse rates and 
potential for scattered showers in NE Zones during the afternoon, 
with the remainder of central Indiana seeing mostly light to 
moderate drizzle "showers". Temperatures are likely to be 35 degrees 
colder Friday afternoon than they were Tuesday afternoon and 
combined with the strong winds, Fall will certainly feel like it has 
arrived!

Friday Night through Wednesday...

Clouds and a few light showers may linger through Friday evening as 
the upper wave axis shifts through the region. Skies will clear late 
Friday night into Saturday morning with winds relaxing as a large 
1030-1035mb surface high moves into the Ohio Valley. The high will 
center over the region Saturday night before shifting to the East 
Coast Sunday and allowing for return southerly flow to commence 
Sunday into early next week. Upper ridging will reestablish for the 
first half of next week with temperatures returning to above normal 
levels. Deep subsidence supports an extended period of mainly clear 
skies Saturday into early next week.

Low level thermals support the coolest daytime temperatures in the 
mid and upper 50s Saturday before recovery back into the low and mid 
70s for the first half of next week. While a lack of boundary layer 
decoupling and lingering cloud coverage will likely limit frost 
accrual to sheltered locales Friday night...confidence remains high 
in a widespread frost for much of the area on Saturday night as lows 
fall into the 30s. Subfreezing temperatures possible for some of our 
normal cool spots as well Saturday night. Frost/Freeze headlines are 
expected to be needed Saturday night. Lows will return to the upper 
40s and early 50s by midweek.
